figures.alt: Residential interior with wood header, adjustable steel temporary support posts, opened framing, and protected floor
figures.caption: A load-bearing wall opening is a structural sequence. The load path, engineered header, temporary support, connections, and final framing need to be resolved before demolition begins.

figures.alt: Commercial space under selective demolition with retained ceiling grid, opened partition bays, and controlled work areas
figures.caption: Controlled demolition exposes existing conditions without getting ahead of the structural plan. Unknown utilities, framing, and interfaces can affect the final scope and price.

figures.alt: Renovation wall rough-in with organized framing, plumbing, electrical boxes, review folder, level, and tape measure
figures.caption: Engineering, permits, and inspections are part of the wall-removal scope. They should be sequenced with the framing work instead of treated as paperwork after the opening is built.
